title: dynamic batching: sequence-length bucketing and padding-minimization heuristics (v7)
author: Aisha Kumar
release_notes: Improved dynamic batching heuristics: smarter seqlen bucketing and padding minimization; 8-12% throughput improvements and reduced padding tokens in canary workloads. No user-visible API changes.
description: Context: continuous batching in the serving runtime currently groups requests by arrival time and simple fixed-length buckets which leaves significant padding waste for mixed-length workloads. This PR implements a refined sequence-length bucketing and padding-minimization heuristic (v7) designed to reduce padding overhead while keeping latency SLOs stable. Motivation: lower per-token cost and increase throughput for realistic, variable-length traffic patterns (chat + completions) without regressing p95 latency. Summary of changes: 1) Dynamic bucket boundary estimator: compute bucket edges using streaming quantiles (p10/p25/p50/p75/p90) with exponential smoothing to adapt to workload shifts. 2) Cost model: introduce a simple padding vs wait latency cost function that evaluates whether to hold a short window (configurable seqlen_wait_threshold_ms) to improve packing. 3) Packing algorithm: primary greedy-first-fit within buckets, fallback to a bounded-knapsack heuristic when residual capacity indicates potential >10% improvement in batch fill. 4) Kernel scheduling hints: pass bucket-based group_size suggestions to the attention/kernel selector so that optimized kernels (grouped-gemm, fused-attn) can be chosen per-batch. 5) KV cache warm-up + reuse tweaks: when sequences share a high prefix similarity score (prefix_hash heuristic) the KV cache is retained and reused aggressively to avoid reallocation cost on repeated prefixes. 6) Metrics & observability: new counters and histograms (seqlen_bucket_profile, padding_waste_tokens, batch_fill_ratio, seqlen_wait_decisions) and a per-route flag to enable/disable the new heuristic at runtime. 7) Tests and benchmarks: added unit tests for bucket boundary computation, packing primitives, and end-to-end perf harness tests; added canary dashboard charts. Checklist: - [x] Algorithm design done and reviewed. - [x] Unit tests added/updated. - [x] Perf harness + canary results attached. - [x] Docs: runtime tuning notes and flags. - [x] Feature gated with runtime flag default=on for standard routes. Rolling considerations: canary was used for three weeks across multiple traffic profiles before merge; heuristics are configurable and can be disabled at route-level. Backwards compatibility: no public API changes; internal config names documented. Operational knobs: seqlen_bucket_profile (auto/manual), seqlen_wait_threshold_ms (default 6ms), padding_waste_target_percent (default 12%), packing_mode (greedy|knapsack). Implementation notes: - The estimator runs in O(1) per request (amortized) using t-digest-like sketch for quantiles to avoid memory blow-up. - The knapsack fallback is bounded (max N=64 items) and runs on batch-assembly path only when beneficial. - Kernel scheduler hooks are advisory; existing kernel selection remains the authority for correctness. - KV cache reuse uses a lightweight prefix hash to avoid full token comparisons and falls back to safe copy on mismatch. Rollout plan: - Start canary on 10% of traffic for latency-sensitive customers, monitor p50/p95/p99 latency and padding_waste_tokens. - If padding_waste reduces without p95 regression, progressively increase. Security and testing: no new network surface; unit tests + stress tests added. See commits and files_changed for details.
commits: 4 commits: (1) estimator: add streaming quantile estimator and bucket profile config; (2) packing: implement greedy and bounded-knapsack fallback; (3) runtime: integrate kernel scheduling hints and seqlen wait logic; (4) tests/docs: add unit tests, perf harness updates and runtime docs.
files_changed: src/runtime/batching/seqlen_bucket_estimator.rs, src/runtime/batching/packer.rs, src/runtime/scheduler/kernel_selector.rs, src/runtime/kv_cache/prefix_reuse.rs, components/metrics/metrics_registry.rs, tests/perf/dynamic_bucketing_canary.py, docs/runtime/tuning.md, examples/benchmarks/packing_profile.yaml, ci/pipeline.yml
benchmarks: Canary results (aggregate over 24h runs): - Mixed-chat workload (avg seq=512, std=420): throughput +9.4%, padding tokens -17.3%, p50 latency +0.8ms, p95 latency +3.7ms. - Long-tail workload (avg seq=1400): throughput +7.1%, padding tokens -12.1%, p95 latency +4.6ms. - Synthetic small-seq workload: no measurable regression. Overall token-cost reduction aligns with padding_waste drop. CPU overhead: +2-3% due to knapsack fallback runs (rare).
review_comments: Initial review (Liam): asked for canary results and configuration defaults; noted potential fairness issues for tiny requests—requested an opt-out flag per route. Author response: added route-level flag, adjusted default seqlen_wait_threshold_ms from 10ms->6ms, added fairness check to avoid starving sub-ms requests. Reviewer (Rosa): requested clearer metrics and dashboards; author added seqlen_wait_decisions histogram and dashboard tiles. Devon: flagged a flaky packing unit test; CI rerun fixed after increasing timeout and adding deterministic seeding. Approvals: Liam (approved), Rosa (approved after changes), Devon (approved).
checks: CI pipeline: lint (pass), unit-tests (pass), integration-tests (pass after 1 rerun for flaky packing_test), perf-harness (pass), security-scan (pass). One flaky test caused a single rerun (packing_test) and was fixed in commit 3 by seeding the RNG deterministically.
notes: This PR is part of the dynamic batching heuristic series (v2..v7) and consolidates prior traffic-adaptive improvements. It targets runtime performance and cost efficiency. Operators can disable per-route if p95 regressions are observed.
example_config_snippet:
seqlen_bucket_profile: auto
seqlen_wait_threshold_ms: 6
padding_waste_target_percent: 12
packing_mode: greedy
